question: What is the primary purpose of qualitative interviews in nursing research?

options.B: To capture lived experiences and perceptions

explanation: Qualitative interviews focus on understanding human experiences, beliefs, and meanings rather than gathering numerical measurements. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: Why are qualitative interviews preferred over closed-ended surveys when exploring complex health topics?

options.A: They allow researchers to explore deep, unanticipated insights
options.B: They take significantly less time to analyze and code
options.C: They eliminate all forms of participant bias instantly
options.D: They require no prior training in human communication

explanation: Open dialogue gives participants room to express complex thoughts that structured surveys cannot accommodate. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h1)

question: Which interview type uses a flexible guide while allowing the researcher to explore emergent topics?
explanation: Semi-structured formats balance prepared questions with the freedom to probe deeper into unexpected responses. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h2)

question: An unstructured interview is best characterized by which feature?

options.A: Interruption by the researcher every two minutes
options.B: A single broad opening question directing the narrative flow
options.C: Strictly numerical data recording during the session
options.D: A rigid sequence of identical questions for every participant

explanation: Unstructured interviews rely on minimal prompting to let participants share their stories naturally. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h2)

question: What is the primary function of an interview guide in qualitative research?

options.A: To replace audio recording devices during fieldwork
options.B: To provide exact answers that participants must memorize
options.C: To keep the research conversation focused on study themes

explanation: The guide serves as a flexible roadmap ensuring all key research objectives are addressed during the session. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h3)

question: Which question demonstrates the best approach for an open-ended qualitative interview?

options.A: Is your blood sugar level higher today than it was yesterday?
options.B: Don't you agree that eating too much sugar causes diabetes?
options.C: How do you feel about managing your diabetes care at home?
options.D: Why do patients always ignore nurse advice on sugar intake?

explanation: This question invites the participant to share their personal perspective without leading them toward a predetermined answer. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h3)

question: What sampling method is most commonly used in qualitative interviews to select informative participants?
explanation: Purposive sampling deliberately selects individuals who have deep experience with the specific phenomenon being investigated. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h4)

question: Why is it important to separate research recruitment from routine clinical care in hospitals?

options.A: To speed up the physical transcription process
options.B: To ensure the hospital makes a profit from the study
options.C: To eliminate the need for formal ethical approval
options.D: To prevent patients from feeling coerced to participate

explanation: Patients might feel pressured to take part if approached by healthcare staff while receiving treatment unless boundaries are clear. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h4)

question: What is a key technique used during an interview to encourage a participant to keep talking?

options.A: Using minimal verbal prompts and nods
options.B: Writing detailed notes instead of listening
options.C: Interrupting to correct factual errors immediately
options.D: Crossing arms to show professional authority

explanation: Small verbal cues and non-verbal nods signal interest and prompt the participant to elaborate further. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h5)

question: Why must a nurse researcher maintain a non-judgmental attitude during a qualitative interview?

options.A: To ensure all answers match statistical averages
options.B: To prevent participants from withholding sensitive information
options.C: To finish the interview session in under ten minutes
options.D: To guarantee that the institutional budget is approved

explanation: Showing judgment or shock closes down communication and stops participants from sharing honest experiences. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h5)

question: What is used to protect participant identity in research transcripts and reports?
explanation: Pseudonyms or false names replace real identifiers to ensure participant anonymity in study documentation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h6)

question: Informed consent in qualitative interviews is best described as which of the following?

options.A: A verbal agreement that binds the patient to finish the study
options.B: A one-time signature signed before reading any study details
options.C: An ongoing process where withdrawal is always allowed
options.D: A legal contract managed entirely by the hospital pharmacist

explanation: Consent is not just a form; it is a continuous agreement, and participants keep the right to stop anytime. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h6)

question: What does verbatim transcription involve during qualitative data processing?

options.A: Summarizing main interview points into bulleted statistics
options.B: Deleting audio files immediately after the interview ends
options.C: Converting audio recordings into exact written text word-for-word
options.D: Translating local dialects into formal English instantly

explanation: Verbatim transcription captures every spoken word, pause, and utterance to maintain data integrity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h7)

question: Why are field notes taken alongside audio recordings during an interview session?

options.A: To capture non-verbal cues and environmental context
options.B: To grade the participant on their communication skills
options.C: To replace the need for an audio recorder entirely
options.D: To give the researcher something to read while resting

explanation: Audio recorders miss body language, expressions, and room dynamics, which field notes successfully record. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h7)

question: What strategy involves taking transcribed interpretations back to participants to confirm accuracy?
explanation: Member checking allows participants to review findings and verify that their original views were represented correctly. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h8)

question: Why is an audit trail important for establishing rigor in qualitative research?

options.A: It documents every methodological decision to prove study credibility
options.B: It proves that all participants shared identical opinions
options.C: It measures the speed at which participants spoke during sessions
options.D: It calculates the exact financial cost of running the interviews

explanation: An audit trail provides a clear log of choices made, enabling others to follow and trust the research process. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h8)
